flags.quote: floating-base forward kinematics (quaternions, Rodrigues' rotations, velocity composition) from joint encoders maps impacts onto the robot mesh, and Khatib's operational-space effective mass estimates impact energy.
flags.issue: Garden-path sentence in the first bullet of the top job. The subject is 13 words long, and 'from joint encoders maps' reads at first as a subject-verb agreement error ('encoders maps'). The bullet also switches from Troy as actor ('Developing') to two inanimate subjects after the colon, so it doesn't match the verb-led bullets around it. It's the first sentence a careful reader parses.
flags.fix: Put 'from joint encoders' next to its noun and split the clauses with a semicolon. This also absorbs the stray MuJoCo clause from bullet 2 (see next flag) at no line cost (tested: still 3 lines): 'Developing rigid-body kinematics, dynamics, and a physics-based MuJoCo simulation for Atlas impacts: floating-base forward kinematics from joint encoders (quaternions, Rodrigues' formula, velocity composition) maps impacts onto the robot mesh; Khatib's operational-space effective mass estimates impact energy.' (BD1-BD4)

flags.quote: validating its filtering against synthetic pulses of known size and measuring its noise floor; building a physics-based MuJoCo impact simulation.
flags.issue: Semicolon misuse and a tense switch inside one bullet. A semicolon should join two independent clauses, but '; building a ...' is a subjectless participial fragment. It also jumps from past ('Designed') to present progressive halfway through, so it reads like two notes pasted together. 'Known size' is also vaguer than the source's 'known amplitude'.
flags.fix: End the bullet at the noise floor and use parallel past-tense verbs: 'Designed a delta-v impact-severity metric robust to sensor bandwidth limits, validated its filtering against synthetic pulses of known amplitude, and measured its noise floor.' (tested: 2 lines, 513 of 517 pt). Move the MuJoCo simulation into bullet 1 as shown above (BD3, BD5, BD6).

flags.quote: model-based tuned with feed-forward and anti-windup (0.8% speed error in simulation), with 10 fault monitors
flags.issue: 'model-based tuned' is ungrammatical: a compound adjective is being used as an adverb on a past participle. The sentence also repeats 'with ... with', and 'designed and implemented' is a wordy doublet.
flags.fix: 'Embedded real-time control: implemented a 1 kHz PI velocity controller in C++ on an ESP32-S3 (FreeRTOS), tuned from a motor model with feed-forward and anti-windup (0.8% speed error in simulation), plus 10 fault monitors, a hardware watchdog, and a kill switch.' (OR2-OR4). Without the run-in label (next flag) this drops from 3 lines to 2 (tested). It breaks at the hard hyphen in 'feed-/forward', which is acceptable.

flags.quote: State estimation: | Verification: | Control: | Embedded real-time control: | Signal processing: | Led a 5-engineer team; | Motion control and optimization:
flags.issue: Bullets aren't parallel. Six Projects bullets open with a run-in label, but the third orthosis bullet ('Led a 5-engineer team;') and every Experience bullet open with a verb. The labels are also set in roman, while the Skills labels are bold, so 'State estimation: built ...' reads as a broken sentence instead of a heading. The labels cost 60 to 140 pt per line, which is what pushes 'update.' into a widow and splits 'closed-/loop' at a line end.
flags.fix: Drop all six labels and open each bullet with a verb (Built / Checked / Ran / Implemented / Cut / Led / Designing). The tested label-free versions fit in 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2 and 2 lines, which saves 2 lines in Projects. If the labels must stay, put the orthosis bullet under one too and set every label in bold to match Skills.

flags.quote: Verification: Jacobians checked against finite differences in GoogleTest unit tests, C++ matched to a Python reference within 1e-13, and observability analysis confirming position and yaw drift while roll, pitch, and velocity stay bounded.
flags.issue: Faulty parallelism inside the series: noun + past participle ('Jacobians checked'), noun + past participle ('C++ matched'), then noun + present participle ('analysis confirming'). It's also the only bullet with no actor. 'confirming position and yaw drift' is a garden path: the reader first takes 'position' as the object of 'confirming'.
flags.fix: 'Checked Jacobians against finite differences in GoogleTest unit tests, matched the C++ filter to a Python reference within 1e-13, and confirmed by observability analysis that position and yaw drift while roll, pitch, and velocity stay bounded.' top3: Three sentences are broken in the most-read blocks. Fix them: BD bullet 1's garden-path subject ('...from joint encoders maps impacts'), BD bullet 2's semicolon followed by a tense-switching fragment ('; building a physics-based MuJoCo impact simulation'), and the orthosis 'model-based tuned'.

Make the Projects bullets parallel. Drop the six run-in labels, which are set in roman and readers take for broken sentences ('Led a 5-engineer team;' has none), and rewrite 'Verification' with active verbs. That alone removes the 'update.' widow and the 'closed-/loop' split, and recovers 2 lines.

Spend the 3 recovered lines (Legged bullet 1, Caterpillar, orthosis bullet 1) on whitespace. Text currently sits 2.3 pt above a 0.4 in bottom margin with about 2.5 pt between entries; go to about 3.5 pt after entries and 6 pt before sections, and make the email, LinkedIn and portfolio links clickable.
